previous_abstract: This paper investigates joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) for grant-free random access in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. We firstly propose a multi-frame transmission scheme with affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) to handle the large differential delay and Doppler shift, and derive the input-output relationship. The scheme exploits the quasi-static property of the channel over consecutive frames to gather more observations for JADCE. Subsequently, we learn a score-based generative channel prior directly on the AFDM effective channel to account for fractional delay and Doppler without restrictive sparse or grid-aligned channel assumptions. Colored Gaussian noise is used in this training to account for correlations in the denoiser input error. With the learned channel prior available, we propose to incorporate it into message passing. This design enables the seamless integration of score-based generative models as a minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoiser. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed receiver outperforms the baseline in terms of activity detection and channel estimation.
current_abstract: This paper investigates joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE) for grant-free random access in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. We firstly propose a multi-frame transmission scheme with affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) to handle the large differential delay and Doppler shift, and derive the input-output relationship. The scheme exploits the quasi-static property of the channel over consecutive frames to gather more observations for JADCE. Subsequently, we learn a score-based generative channel prior directly on the AFDM effective channel with fractional delay and Doppler, without restrictive sparse or grid-aligned channel assumptions. The training uses colored Gaussian noise to account for correlations in the denoiser input error. With the learned channel prior available, we employ a turbo message passing (TMP) framework that models the entire channel matrix as a super node, rather than factorizing it element-wise. This design enables the seamless integration of score-based generative models as a minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoiser. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed receiver outperforms the original score-based TMP receiver in terms of activity detection and channel estimation.
